THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.MC.No. 1800 of 2015 2  ORDER
The petitioner herein is the 6 th accused in S.T.No.1599 of 2004 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ernakulam.

The said proceeding was based on a complaint lodged by the Food Inspector arraying as many as 9 persons alleging commission of offence punishable under Sections 2(ia)(a),(m), 7(i) and 7(v) r/w. Section 16(i)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Appendix B item No.A.11.01.11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1957.
2.
According to the prosecution, the 1st accused is the vendor, 2nd accused is the licensee and accused Nos.3 to 6 are the partners of the 7th accused, the firm.
The accused No.8 and 9 are the persons from whom the vendor had purchased toned milk.
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the proceedings against the accused Nos.3, 4 and 5 were quashed by this Court by Annexure-A2 order dated 14.9.2012.
This was based on the premise that there were no pleading in the complainant that the partners were in charge and responsible for the day to day conduct of the firm.
The petitioner has also been arrayed in his capacity as the partner of the firm and hence the proceedings against him are also liable to be quashed is the submission.
4. Heard the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. I have considered the submissions advanced.

6. In Paragraph No.3 of Annexure-A2, this Court, while quashing the proceedings against accused Nos. 2 to 5, had occasion to observe as follows:
"3. The factual foundation of pleading that petitioners were in charge of the business of the firm is conspicuously absent in the complaint.
It cannot be supplied by amendment of the complaint.
Without there being a foundation by necessary pleading in the complaint, there cannot be proof, the petitioner's counsel submits.
In order to fasten liability on the partners, it must be clearly alleged in the complaint that they were in charge of and were responsible to the Company/ firm for the conduct of the business.
That omission in the complaint is fatal.
As such proceedings in S.T.Case 1599/2004 of Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam as against these petitioners will stand quashed."

7. Being arrayed as the accused as one of the partners, those observations would apply to the petitioner on all fours.
8. In that view of the matter, this petition is liable to be allowed.
All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.T. No. 1599 of 2004 on the file of the CJM, Ernakulam will stand quashed.

Sd/-
